p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The four rules every manual test must satisfy, each with a short worked fragment.

p.sibling-document-pointers: The rationale for the tier lives in [`MANUAL-TESTS-PROTOCOL.xml`](MANUAL-TESTS-PROTOCOL.xml); the copy-ready skeleton that bakes these rules in lives in [`test-template.xml`](test-template.xml).

p.A-WALKTHROUGH-THAT-BREAKS-ANY-OF-THESE-I: A walkthrough that breaks any of these is a bug in the test, not a property of the product it exercises.

clean-slate.title: Rule 1 — Clean slate is mandatory

p.EVERY-RUN-STARTS-FROM-NOTHING-AND-TOUCHE: Every run starts from nothing and touches no real user state.

facts.MECHANISM-A-SCRATCH-PROJECT: **A scratch project** created fresh with `mktemp -d`, so the working tree the test operates on is disposable and unique per run.
facts.MECHANISM-AN-ENVIRONMENT-REDIRECT: **An environment redirect** pointing the tool's per-user state (cache, config, home) into that scratch, so the real per-user directory is never read from or written to.

clean-slate.fence: export SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d)" export TOOL_HOME="$SCRATCH/tool-home" # redirect the tool's per-user state export PROJECT="$SCRATCH/project" mkdir -p "$TOOL_HOME" "$PROJECT" cd "$PROJECT"

p.now-every-command-reads-and-writes-under: Now every command the tool runs reads and writes under `$SCRATCH`.

p.nothing-under-the-real-home-is-at-risk: Nothing under the developer's real home is at risk, and two runs on the same machine cannot collide.

p.A-TEST-THAT-MUTATES-REAL-USER-STATE-IS-A: **A test that mutates real user state is a bug in the test**, even if every step passes — because the next contributor's run inherits that mutation and the walkthrough is no longer reproducible.

p.A-STEP-THAT-SEEMS-TO-NEED-REAL-STATE-MEA: If a step seems to *need* the real per-user directory, the redirect is wrong or incomplete; fix the redirect.

self-contained.title: Rule 2 — Self-contained walkthrough

p.A-READER-OPENS-ONE-FILE-AND-NEEDS-NOTHIN: A reader opens exactly one file, executes it top to bottom, and needs nothing else — no companion doc, no tribal knowledge, no "ask whoever wrote this".

p.THE-FILE-NAMES-ITS-OWN-PRECONDITIONS-AND: The file names its own preconditions and provides its own setup.

p.EVERY-STEP-IS-A-COMMAND-BLOCK-PLUS-AN-EX: Every step is a **command block plus an "Expected" paragraph**.

p.THE-COMMAND-IS-COPY-PASTEABLE-THE-EXPECT: The command is copy-pasteable; the Expected states the observable outcome in enough detail that a reader can tell pass from fail without guessing.

self-contained.fence:
3. Initialise the project.
``` acme init ```
**Expected.** The command exits 0 and prints `Initialised acme project at <path>`. A config file now exists at `$TOOL_HOME/config.toml`; `cat` it and confirm it names the current directory as the project root.

p.A-COMMAND-WITH-NO-EXPECTED-IS-NOT-A-TEST: A command with no Expected is not a test step — it cannot pass or fail.

p.if-you-cannot-articulate-the-outcome-you: If you cannot articulate the outcome, you do not yet know what the step proves.

p.WRITE-THE-EXPECTED-FIRST-THEN-THE-COMMAN: Write the Expected first, then the command that earns it.

platform.title: Rule 3 — Platform coverage

p.COMMANDS-ARE-POSIX-SHELL-COMPATIBLE: Commands are **POSIX-shell compatible** so the walkthrough runs on every platform a contributor might use.

p.NAME-ONE-PRIMARY-PLATFORM-AND-ADD-A-PORT: Name one **primary platform** — the environment the author actually runs the test in — and show its form first; where output legitimately differs across platforms, add a short portable note rather than a second full transcript.

platform.fence:
5. Show the built artifact's path.
``` acme where --bin ```
**Expected (primary platform).** Prints `$PROJECT/target/acme.exe`.
**Portable note.** On macOS and Linux there is no `.exe` suffix — the path ends in `/acme`. Path separators and any `stat`-style flags differ likewise; the trailing component and exit code are what the step checks.

p.divergences-worth-a-note-lead: Divergences worth a note are the usual ones:

p.KEEP-THE-CHECK-PLATFORM-INDEPENDENT: Keep the *check* platform-independent (exit code, the meaningful substring) and let the note absorb the cosmetic difference.

exit.title: Rule 4 — Exit discipline

p.EVERY-WALKTHROUGH-ENDS-WITH-TWO-FIXED-SE: Every walkthrough ends with two fixed sections.

p.SECTION-A-COPY-PASTEABLE-TEARDOWN-BLOCK: **A copy-pasteable teardown block** that removes everything the run created — the whole point of the clean-slate setup is that one command returns the machine to its pre-run state:

exit.fence:
## Teardown
``` rm -rf "$SCRATCH" unset SCRATCH TOOL_HOME PROJECT ```

p.TEARDOWN-IS-A-SINGLE-RM-RF: Because all state lives under `$SCRATCH` (Rule 1), teardown is a single `rm -rf` — no hunting through the real per-user directory for stray files.

p.TEARDOWN-REACHING-OUTSIDE-THE-SCRATCH-ME: If teardown needs to reach outside `$SCRATCH`, Rule 1 was violated somewhere above.

p.SECTION-A-WHAT-TO-FILE-IF-IT-FAILS-LIST: **A "what to file if it fails" list** naming the artifacts a follow-up session needs to diagnose a divergence, so the reader collects them *before* running teardown destroys the evidence:

exit.fence:
## What to file if it fails
- The failing step number and how the actual output differed from Expected (paste both). - Verbose logs: re-run the failing command with the tool's debug flag or log env var set. - The consumer-facing artifact under test (lockfile, export, manifest) as produced — its exact bytes, not a paraphrase. - Platform, tool version, and shell.

facts.SUM-CLEAN-SLATE: **Clean slate:** `mktemp -d` project plus an env redirect for the tool's per-user state; touching real state is a bug in the test.
facts.SUM-SELF-CONTAINED: **Self-contained:** one file, top to bottom, nothing else needed; every step is a command block plus an Expected paragraph.
facts.SUM-PLATFORM-COVERAGE: **Platform coverage:** POSIX commands, primary platform first, a portable note where output differs cosmetically.
facts.SUM-EXIT-DISCIPLINE: **Exit discipline:** a one-command teardown of `$SCRATCH`, and a what-to-collect list gathered before teardown runs.
